يَدَيْهِ:
Meaning *"his two hands"*, it comes from *يَد (yad)*, meaning *hand*, in the dual form with the suffix *-hi*, referring to two hands belonging to someone.

In Qur'anic Arabic, it often appears in expressions with broader meanings. The phrase *بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ (bayna yadayhi)*, literally *"between his two hands"*, is a common idiom meaning *before him*, *in front of him*, or *that which already precedes him*. Accordingly, when the Qur'an speaks of confirming *مَا بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ*, classical commentators understood it as referring to earlier scriptures already present at the time.
